key_insight: LLMPopSim shows that AI agent populations can approximate real community health behaviors, but accuracy is uneven across places and outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This could help public health teams simulate screening patterns and test interventions at the community level before real-world rollout.
method: Built AI agent populations using U.S. Census and CDC data.
Trained on Hawaii 2018 data and tested on held-out 2022 cohorts from Hawaii and New York State.
Compared simulated vs observed colorectal cancer screening and mammography at the ZCTA level.
evidence_signal: Across four evaluations, mean absolute error was 3.5 to 15.0 percentage points and ZCTA-level correlations ranged from 0.26 to 0.69.
watch_item: Performance was weakest in lower-prevalence communities, highlighting calibration and subgroup fidelity concerns before practical use.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
